Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg, EDSA corner Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City LEGAL SERVICE DILG OPINION NO. 97 S. 2010 .JUN Z 2 2010 AVIV. ANSELMO B. ADRIANO Sangguniang Bayan Member Santa Maria, Bulacan Dear Hon. Adriano: This refers to your letter seeking our opinion on the legal implications on the refusal of your Mayor to implement an ordinance. You represented that on April 27, 2009, the Sangguniang Bayan (SB) of Santa Maria, Bulacan, enacted Ordinance No. 319, series of 2009, containing the supplemental budget for various expenditures of your municipality, which was duly approved by the Mayor. Notwithstanding the lapse of 90 days from the date of submission of the Ordinance to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan (SP), the SP failed to act on it. In the meantime, the Mayor refused to implement the Ordinance. On September IO, 2009, the SB received a Certification dated September 09, 2009 issued by the SP stating that the Ordinance has been deemed approved. • Nevertheless, the Mayor still refuses to implement the Ordinance alleging that he could be held liable for illegal disbursement of funds. Thus, you now seek our opinion on the following questions: I. "May the Municipal Mayor validly refuse the implementation of Ordinance No. 319? 2. If the answer is in the negative, what legal remedies may be undertaken to immediately implement Ordinance No. 319? 3. What disciplinary actions may be taken, if any, against the Municipal Mayor for his refusal to implement a validly legislated local law?" Anent your first question, we invite your attention to Section 320 of the Local Government Code, to wit: "SEC. 320. Effectivity of Budgets.- The ordinance enacting the annual budget shall take effect at the beginning of the ensuing ca lendar year. An ordinance enacting a supplemental budget, however, shall take effect upon its approval or on the date fixed therein. The responsibility for the execution of the annual and supplemental budgets and the accountability

-2- therefor shall be vested primarily in the local chief executive concerned. " From the foregoing, there is no dispute that Ordinance No. 319, being a supplemental budget, took effect on the date of its approval. that is, on April 27, 2009. Please note that this is specifically provided for in Section 3 of the said Ordinance. Such approval of Ordinance No. 319, series of 2009, was duly certified by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. With this and taking into account the aforequoted provision of the Code, the Mayor, being the Local Chief Executive concerned, has since then been responsible for the execution and implementation of Ordinance No. 319, series of 2009, and is even accountable therefor. Thus, the Mayor cannot validly refuse the implementation of the Ordinance. Anent your second question, we are of the view that an action for mandamus before a court of law pursuant to the Rules of Court is proper. This is because, as explained above. the Mayor is without any discretion to decide on whether or not to implement Ordinance No. 319, series of 2009. Anent your third query, we are of the view that the refusal of the Mayor to implement Ordinance No. 319. series of 2009. if unjustified, may result to a liability for dereliction/neglect of duty. For this purpose, an administrative case may be filed before the Office of the Ombudsman, which is the proper forum to resolve the matter. We hope we have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours. By Authority of the Secretary: AVIV. Legal: La Director Rene L. Brion DILG Region Ill San Fernando City. Pampanga The Municipal Local Gov•t. Operations Officer DILG Municipal Field Office Santa Maria. Bulacan US B. DOQUE lv Di ctor Ill
